sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Built an LSTM forecasting model that predicts CNC machine sensor readings ahead of time, giving the maintenance team early warning of potential spindle issues before they cause unplanned downtime.

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: The existing preventive maintenance schedule was time-based and couldn't catch failures that happened between service windows. Unexpected breakdowns disrupted production and delivery timelines.

sections.heading: Approach
bullets: Sensor telemetries resampled to uniform intervals.
Sliding lookback/horizon windows convert the time series into supervised learning samples.
Sequence-to-sequence LSTM trained with Huber loss and early stopping.
Configurable parameters can be tuned without code changes.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: +40-50% forecast reliability over period-based maintenance. Delivered as a proof-of-concept pipeline with a simulation dashboard for internal review.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Developed a real-time computer vision system that automatically inspects assembled components on the production line and classifies them as pass/fail, replacing manual visual checks.

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Visual quality inspection was done manually by operators - fatigue and subjective judgment led to inconsistent results, with defective units occasionally passing through. Recording inspection outcomes was slow and paper-based.

sections.heading: Approach
bullets: Images captured via production-line cameras.
Dataset annotated and augmented in Roboflow.
Trained a YOLOv11 instance-segmentation model to detect multiple assembly checkpoints.
A Python inspection program reads the live camera feed, runs inference, and tracks component status across frames with a locking mechanism to prevent flicker.
Signals the line controller when all checkpoints pass; supports model switching so one station can handle multiple product variants.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: −50-70% manual inspection effort. Deployed and trialed across multiple production lines.

prostate_cancer_research.title: Race-Aware ML for Prostate Cancer Detection
prostate_cancer_research.subtitle: A two-year, four-paper research program on bias-conscious genomic diagnostics.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: A two-year research program investigating race-specific ML approaches for prostate cancer detection and staging. Gene expression and DNA methylation patterns differ across racial groups, and models trained on mixed-race data can embed bias.

The four papers progressively build a race-aware, feature-optimized diagnostic framework - from SVM binary detection through Gaussian NB and Logistic Regression, culminating in an MLP for cancer-stage classification with explainable AI (SHAP/LIME).

sections.heading: Datasets
paragraphs: TCGA-PRAD (The Cancer Genome Atlas - Prostate Adenocarcinoma) via the UCSC Xena Browser: 554 samples, race-stratified (White majority; Black/African American and Asian minorities).
bullets: Gene expression: RNA-seq HTSeq-Counts (~60K genes, log2(count+1) normalized).
DNA methylation: Illumina HumanMethylation450 (~485K CpG sites).
Race-specific splits for training; external validation on minority cohorts.

sections.heading: Research Timeline
bullets: JMIR Bioinformatics & Biotechnology (2025) - SVM binary cancer detection with DEG + ROC + MSigDB pathway-verified feature selection.
PeerJ Computer Science - Gaussian Naive Bayes detection with 96 scenario combinations and LIME interpretability.
Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis (2025) - Logistic Regression on a 9-gene subset validated against KEGG/GSEA clinical pathways; fairness analysis across racial groups.
JMIR Formative Research (2026) - MLP stage classification (Early I-II vs Late III-IV) from DNA methylation data; DMP + RFE feature selection; SHAP + LIME explainability.
